as_told.title: Narrator clip: the commander in trance sends the group to the window

plain: This story is set in 1959 at the National Photographic Interpretation Center, a US government office in Washington, D.C., where analysts studied photographs. A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron tells it on a podcast with the host Jesse Michels. He says the office's head, Arthur Lundahl, became famous for a session in which an alien was channelled, meaning someone spoke for it while in a trance, and he names others such as Frances Swan and Wilbert Smith. Later in the same conversation Cameron dates it to July 9, 1959 and cites an eleven-page memo about the meeting. According to Cameron, the messages began as automatic writing, written by hand without conscious control. Then they turned to a spoken voice, Lundahl asked for proof, and the voice told them to go to the window. Cameron says they did, and a flying saucer flew past in front of the Capitol building. A narrator on the episode tells it more cautiously: he calls the channelled being 'the commander' and says the group only supposedly saw a UFO. If true, it would mean government staff got a direct sign from non-humans.
